'''Bianca L. Viray''' (born 1983) is an American [[mathematician]] and professor at the [[University of Washington]] in [[Seattle]]. She works in [[arithmetic geometry]], which is a blend of [[algebraic geometry]] and [[algebraic number theory]].

==Education==
Viray received a B.S. in mathematics (cum laude) from the University of Maryland in 2005.<ref name=":cv">{{cite web |title=Bianca Viray CV |url=https://sites.math.washington.edu/~bviray/bvirayCV.pdf |publisher=University of Washington |accessdate=3 November 2020}}</ref>  She received a Ph.D. in mathematics from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 2010; her thesis advisor was [[Bjorn Poonen]].<ref name="mg">{{mathgenealogy|id=154955}}</ref> After receiving her degree, Viray became a Tamarkin Assistant Professor and [[National Science Foundation]] (NSF) Postdoc<ref name="amspostdoc">{{cite web |title=NSF Postdoctoral Fellows Awarded |url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=872 |website=The Latest |publisher=American Mathematical Society |accessdate=3 November 2020}}</ref> at [[Brown University]]; she was at Brown from 2010 to 2014.<ref name=":cv" />

==Career and recognition==
Viray started at the University of Washington as an assistant professor in 2014 and was promoted to associate professor in 2017 and full professor in 2021. She serves on the Board of Girls' Angle, a math club and magazine for girls.<ref name="girls angle">{{cite web |title=Girls' Angle Leadership |url=http://girlsangle.org/page/leadership.html |website=Girls' Angle |accessdate=6 November 2020}}</ref> She received an NSF CAREER Award in 2016.<ref name="NSF">{{cite web |title=CAREER: Rational Points via Asymptotics and Geometry |url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1553459 |website=NSF Award Search |publisher=National Science Foundation |accessdate=3 November 2020}}</ref><ref name="nsf2">{{cite web |title=Bianca Viray awarded an NSF CAREER grant |url=https://math.washington.edu/news/2016/03/01/bianca-viray-awarded-nsf-career-grant |website=Department of Mathematics News & Events |publisher=University of Washington |accessdate=3 November 2020}}</ref> She was selected in fall 2017 to deliver the [[University of Oregon]] Distinguished Lecture for their [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] Student Chapter.<ref name="uo awm">{{cite web |title=Speaker Series |url=https://pages.uoregon.edu/uoawm/speakers.html |website=Association for Women in Mathematics: University of Oregon |accessdate=6 November 2020}}</ref>
She was selected as a Simons Fellow in mathematics in 2020.<ref name="simons">{{cite web |title=Simons Fellows in Mathematics |url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/grant/simons-fellows-in-mathematics/?tab=awardees/ |publisher=Simons Foundation |accessdate=3 November 2020}}</ref> She was elected a [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]] in the class of 2021. Her citation was "''for contributions to arithmetic geometry, in particular to the subject of rational points on varieties, and for sustained efforts to support underrepresented groups in mathematics''".<ref name="AMSfelllow">{{cite web |title=2021 Class of Fellows of the AMS |url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi |publisher=American Mathematical Society |accessdate=3 November 2020}}</ref> She was named to the 2022 class of Fellows of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], "for her leadership and support of women and girls in math through her work on Girl’s Angle, the Women In Numbers research network, the Noetherian Ring, the Western Algebraic Geometry Symposium, and for launching new and impactful mentoring programs".<ref>{{cite web|title=2022 AWM Fellows|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|url=https://awm-math.org/awards-awm-fellows-2022-awm-fellows/}}</ref>
Viray received the 2022-2023 American Mathematical Society Joan and Joseph Birman Fellowship, a fellowship  "that gives exceptionally talented women extra research support during their mid-career years."<ref name=birman>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=6982|title=Bianca Viray receives 2022-2023 Birman Fellowship|publisher=American Mathematical Society|accessdate=7 March 2022}}</ref> She is a former [[American Mathematical Society]] Council member at large.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Committees |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref> She currently serves as the [[American Mathematical Society|AMS]] Vice President.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Officers |url=https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/officers/officers |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>
